_comment: Per-pocket-dimension crafting rules, enforced at the bench by PocketQuests' CraftingMenuMixin.
Patterns match the crafting RESULT's item id; a trailing * wildcards. Covers the crafting table
AND the 2x2 grid. Does NOT cover furnaces, smithing tables, stonecutters or modded machines.
PREMISE PROTECTION ONLY. The hub is the union of eleven packs, so every pocket dimension can
suddenly see 91-129 namespaces its own pack never had. Denying all of those was considered and
rejected: it invents rules the originals never had and produces dead ends across 290 mods.
The rule here is narrower - deny only where craftability defeats the premise, and derive it
from what each standalone pack actually shipped rather than from taste.
hub      - ['*']. A creative lobby; nothing should be crafted there at all.
horror   - 91 namespaces. Its standalone deliberately stripped 111 mods to keep you
under-equipped, and that scarcity IS the premise.
oneblock - exdeorum. Its standalone deliberately dropped Ex Deorum; sieves are a second
resource ladder that undercuts 'the block is the only source'.
survival, lostcities, gauntlet - exdeorum. These three are the 161-jar exploration group and
none of their standalone packs had Ex Deorum. In the hub they can otherwise sieve
dirt for diamonds, which is a strict shortcut past the ore-mining progression they
were built around. Verified against their quest chapters first: zero references to
exdeorum in any of them, so nothing is gated behind a recipe this blocks.
The five block packs share one identical 124-jar base and all own Ex Deorum legitimately, so
they stay unrestricted. The exploration group's own mods (Twilight Forest, the Aether, Iron's
Spellbooks) are NOT denied to the block packs: their items need materials from dimensions
PocketWorlds already refuses entry to, so they gate themselves.
